content.user_title: Create a Signal Tower Story Chapter
content.value_statement: Writing an emotional survival chapter can be difficult when technical action and character choices must work together. This guide provides a staged signal-tower scenario with dialogue, branching outcomes, and ethical decisions.
actual_capabilities: Provides a five-stage structure for planning, building, transmitting, and reflecting.
Supplies bilingual dialogue beats for the character Stella Chen.
Describes fictional tower components, power constraints, and improvised engineering.
Offers branches for Earth contact, an unknown signal, or technical failure.
Frames a choice about sharing survival facts, alien life, and planetary resources.
limitations: It is a fictional writing guide, not an engineering manual.
It does not operate hardware, send radio signals, or contact external services.
The supplied dialogue is mainly Chinese with embedded English phrases.
It covers one chapter and depends on related chapters for the wider story.

use_cases.title: Draft an interactive survival chapter
use_cases.description: Use the stages and dialogue beats to write a character-led chapter about restoring long-range contact.

use_cases.title: Run a science-fiction roleplay scene
use_cases.description: Guide a player through gathering materials, building a tower, and choosing what a rescue message reveals.

use_cases.title: Plan a branching narrative sequence
use_cases.description: Adapt the three outcomes to connect a contact attempt with later rescue, exploration, or settlement scenes.

prompt_templates.title: Start the chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Repairing Signal Tower to begin the planning stage. Write Stella Chen as hopeful but uncertain. End by asking the player whether the project is worth attempting.

prompt_templates.title: Build the tower
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the resource and engineering stages to write a scene where Stella builds a signal tower from damaged equipment and fictional crystals. Keep the technical language believable but clearly fictional.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the message
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the transmission stage to present Stella with a choice: report only survival facts or disclose discoveries on Gaia. Give the player two clear options and their likely consequences.

prompt_templates.title: Create a custom outcome
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Repairing Signal Tower to create a new response branch. Preserve Stella’s emotional conflict, include one unexpected signal detail, and end with a decision that leads into the next chapter.

output_examples.input: Begin the planning stage and ask the player for advice.
output: Stella examines the damaged communications panel and lists the missing parts.
She explains that a high hill could improve the signal.
She asks the player whether they should begin a risky week-long project.
The tower receives a weak confirmation from Mission Control.
Interference ends the exchange before a rescue schedule is certain.
Stella feels relief, then prepares to survive while waiting.
The scanner receives a patterned reply from an unexplored region.
Stella identifies the response as nonhuman but cannot judge its intent.
The player chooses whether to investigate or protect the camp.

best_practices: State that the engineering details are fictional when adapting them for public content.
Let the player make the disclosure decision instead of selecting it without consent.
Use each branch to create a clear link to the next story chapter.
anti_patterns: Do not present the fictional tower construction as real radio or electrical safety guidance.
Do not remove the player choice from the message disclosure dilemma.
Do not treat a contact outcome as a guaranteed rescue.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create an interactive science-fiction chapter about repairing a signal tower and seeking contact.

faq.question: Does it send real communications?
faq.answer: No. It contains narrative prompts only and cannot operate equipment or send messages.

faq.question: Is the engineering information real?
faq.answer: No. The tower, crystals, and biological components are fictional story devices.

faq.question: Which language does the source use?
faq.answer: The source uses Chinese dialogue with embedded English phrases and labels.

faq.question: Can I choose a different ending?
faq.answer: Yes. You can adapt the listed branches or create a new response that fits your story.

faq.question: Who is the main character?
faq.answer: The guide centers on Stella Chen, a stranded survivor deciding how to reconnect with Earth.
